details:
Q1: What code changes does this issue deliver? The pipeline cannot start a heal issue through intake itself; that needs a reporter dispatch with verified failed-run metadata.
Choices:
A) Both changes, on this issue: (1) the intake refuses to file a heal issue when `heal-scope render` produces an empty or invalid marker, and reports an intake defect instead; (2) the rejection-category diagnostics. Re-filing waits for the next real failure to go through intake. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Only the rejection-category diagnostics. The intake keeps filing heal issues that have no marker.
C) Only the intake fail-closed marker guard. No diagnostics change.
Q2: Which rejection path should report the new bounded, path-safe categories? #6866's plan is not available here.
Choices:
A) The review sandbox snapshot/transfer in `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`. Rejections that today fall back to legacy codes or `reason=unknown` get a fixed `category=` token. Existing `reason=` tokens stay unchanged. (RECOMMENDED)
B) The heal isolated editor transfer in `scripts/heal_isolated_implement.sh:131-133`. Today every transfer rejection collapses to `reason=out_of_heal_scope`; it would carry the underlying transfer reason and category through, alongside the existing token.
C) Both A and B.
**Note:** Q1:C (no diagnostics) makes this question moot.
Q3: Should this run also re-dispatch a heal report for #6866's failed runs?
Choices:
A) No. This issue only delivers code and tests. #6866 stays as-is, and no marker is copied or edited in. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Yes. Add a one-off step that re-reports #6866's runs to intake. This needs the verified run IDs from #6866 to be pasted into this issue.
